topic: Weech formula — birth weight and height
title: Weech formula — birth weight and height
definition: Formulas for estimating pediatric weight and height.
keyPoints: Weech (weight kg): age(y)x2+8 for 3-12 y; (age mo+9)/2 for 3-12 mo; age(y)x7-5)/2 for 1-6
Height: 2.5 cm/mo 0-6 mo; 1.25 cm/mo 6-12; age(y)x6+77 for >2 y
Double birth weight by 5 mo, triple by 1 y, quadruple by 2.5 y
pearls: Broselow tape preferred in real emergencies.
clinicalContext: 5-y-old emergency resuscitation, weight unknown.
nursingPriority: Weech: 5x2+8 = 18 kg; calculate drug doses.

title: Gomez classification of malnutrition
clinicalContext: 2-y-old at 60% expected weight.
nursingPriority: Gomez grade III severe malnutrition; refer NRC, evaluate for complications, feeding plan.

topic: Fetal weight — Johnson, Shepard, Hadlock formulas
title: Fetal weight — Johnson, Shepard, Hadlock formulas
keyPoints: Johnson (clinical): EFW (g) = (SFH in cm - n) x 155; n=12 if vertex above ischial spine, 11 if at/below
Hadlock: USG BPD + HC + AC + FL — most accurate
clinicalContext: SFH 36 cm, station -2.
nursingPriority: Johnson EFW = (36-12)x155 = 3720 g.

title: Teeth eruption timeline
keyPoints: Primary: lower central incisors 6-10 mo, first molars 13-19 mo, canines 16-22, 2nd molars 23-33 mo; complete 20 teeth by 3 y
Permanent 1st molars at 6 y, wisdom teeth 17-21 y
clinicalContext: 7-mo-old has first tooth eruption.
nursingPriority: Lower central incisor — reassure, teach gentle cleaning with cloth, cold teething ring.

title: Fontanel closure
definition: Membranous gaps at skull suture junctions.
keyPoints: Delayed closure: rickets, hypothyroidism, hydrocephalus, Down
Bulging: raised ICP, meningitis, dehydration can sink
clinicalContext: 2-mo-old post-viral illness has sunken fontanel.
nursingPriority: Sign of dehydration — assess hydration, feeding, IV fluids if severe.

title: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)
definition: See chn-5. ICDS services at AWC.
keyPoints: 6 services: supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-up, referral, pre-school education, nutrition-health education
clinicalContext: AWW at AWC.
nursingPriority: Deliver 6 ICDS services; conduct growth monitoring monthly.

title: Height measurement technique
keyPoints: Head in Frankfort plane; heels, buttocks, scapula touch board
clinicalContext: 3-y-old for routine check.
nursingPriority: Measure standing height with stadiometer in Frankfort plane, plot on growth chart.

title: Developmental milestones
keyPoints: Social smile: 6-8 wk; head hold: 3 mo
Roll over: 5 mo; sit with support: 6 mo, without 8
Crawl 9 mo, stand with support 9, cruise 10-11, walk 12-15
First word: 1 y; 2-word sentence: 2 y; pedal tricycle: 3 y
clinicalContext: 9-mo-old not sitting independently.
nursingPriority: Developmental delay concern — detailed history, physical exam, refer for intervention if delay confirmed.

title: Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome)
keyPoints: Features: upslanting palpebral fissures, Brushfield spots, simian crease, sandal gap, hypotonia, short neck
Associations: AV canal defect (40%), duodenal atresia, hypothyroidism, ALL risk, Alzheimer early
Screening: quad marker (low AFP, low uE3, high hCG, high inhibin)
clinicalContext: Newborn with facial dysmorphism and poor tone.
nursingPriority: Karyotype to confirm, echocardiogram for AV canal, TSH screen, early intervention, parental counseling.

title: Cystic fibrosis
keyPoints: Affects lungs (recurrent pneumonia, bronchiectasis), pancreas (malabsorption), sweat glands (salty)
Treatment: airway clearance, pancreatic enzymes, fat-soluble vitamins, CFTR modulators
clinicalContext: Recurrent pneumonia + failure to thrive + salty sweat.
nursingPriority: Sweat chloride test to confirm; pulmonology referral, airway clearance, pancreatic enzymes, fat-soluble vit supplementation.

title: Patau syndrome (Trisomy 13)
definition: Trisomy 13 — severe anomalies, most die in infancy.
keyPoints: Holoprosencephaly, midline cleft lip/palate, polydactyly, cardiac defects, cutis aplasia
clinicalContext: Newborn with cleft lip, cardiac defect, polydactyly.
nursingPriority: Karyotype, genetic counseling, discuss with family about goals of care, supportive care.

title: Malnutrition — SAM and MAM
keyPoints: SAM: W/H <-3 Z OR MUAC <11.5 cm OR bilateral pitting edema
MAM: W/H -3 to -2 Z OR MUAC 11.5-12.5
clinicalContext: 2-y-old MUAC 10.8 cm, bilateral pitting edema, anorexia.
nursingPriority: SAM with complications — admit to NRC/SNCU, start F-75 (stabilization), treat infections, electrolytes (K, Mg), vit A, gradual transition to F-100.

title: Indicators of malnutrition
clinicalContext: 5-y-old with W/H -3 Z.
nursingPriority: Severe wasting — acute malnutrition management, MUAC check, nutrition support.

title: Calorie intake of 1-year-old
keyPoints: Formula: 100 kcal/kg first 10 kg, 50/kg next 10, 20/kg thereafter
clinicalContext: 10 kg 1-y-old.
nursingPriority: Needs ~1000 kcal/day; balanced IYCF: continued breastfeeding, 3 meals + 2 snacks of family food.

title: Nutritional status assessment
keyPoints: Clinical: pallor, edema, Bitot spots, hair changes
Biochemical: Hb, albumin, prealbumin, vit levels
clinicalContext: OPD child screening.
nursingPriority: Plot W/H on growth chart, measure MUAC, clinical exam for pallor/edema, review dietary intake.

title: Kwashiorkor
keyPoints: Bilateral pitting edema, flag-sign hair, moon facies, hepatomegaly, irritable-apathetic mood
Treatment: F-75 stabilization → F-100, monitor refeeding syndrome
clinicalContext: 3-y-old with pitting edema, hair depigmentation, distended abdomen.
nursingPriority: SAM-kwashiorkor — admit, F-75 cautious feeding, monitor for refeeding (P, Mg, K drop), vit A, zinc, deworm.

title: Vitamin A prophylaxis — doses
keyPoints: 12-59 mo: 200,000 IU q6 mo (first dose with 1st MR dose)
Signs of deficiency: night blindness, Bitot spots, xerosis, keratomalacia
clinicalContext: 2-y-old at Vit A day.
nursingPriority: Administer 200,000 IU oral single dose, document card, next dose 6 mo.

title: Rickets
keyPoints: Vit D deficiency in growing bone
Vit D3 60,000 IU weekly x6-8 wk + Ca
clinicalContext: 18-mo breastfed child on vegetarian mother with bowed legs.
nursingPriority: Vit D3 60,000 IU weekly + calcium; sunlight; diet.

title: Neonatal period definition
keyPoints: Components of mortality: prematurity, birth asphyxia, sepsis
clinicalContext: Item on neonatal period definition.
nursingPriority: First 28 days of life — classify mortality as NMR.

title: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC)
keyPoints: Criteria: stable LBW, no severe illness
Upright chest-to-chest position, diapered only, head turned
Continuous or intermittent; aim >=1 h at a time
Benefits: thermoregulation, breastfeeding, weight gain, decreased mortality
clinicalContext: 1.4 kg preterm stable.
nursingPriority: Initiate KMC — baby skin-to-skin on mother's chest, upright, covered with blanket, continuous as tolerated, monitor vitals initially.

title: Breastfeeding — positions and exclusivity
definition: Exclusive BF 0-6 mo, continue to 2 y with complementary.
keyPoints: Good attachment: chin touching breast, wide mouth, areola more visible above
clinicalContext: 2-day-old baby with poor attachment and sore maternal nipples.
nursingPriority: Teach cross-cradle position, assess latch, chin touches breast with lower lip everted and mouth wide; correct attachment; check for tongue-tie.

title: Regurgitation vs vomiting
keyPoints: Regurgitation: small amount, effortless, common in infants
clinicalContext: 6-wk-old with projectile non-bilious vomiting after feeds.
nursingPriority: Pyloric stenosis — USG pyloric muscle, correct hypochloremic alkalosis, plan Ramstedt pyloromyotomy.

title: Thermoregulation in neonates
definition: Newborns cold-stress prone — large SA, low fat.
keyPoints: Mechanisms of loss: evaporation, conduction, convection, radiation
4 warm chain: WHO — delivery room warm, immediate dry, skin-to-skin, warm transport
clinicalContext: Newborn axillary T 35.8°C.
nursingPriority: Moderate hypothermia — dry, skin-to-skin with mother under warm blanket, monitor T q30 min, check blood sugar.

title: Temperature regulation in neonates
clinicalContext: Item on brown fat.
nursingPriority: Brown fat (interscapular, axillae, around kidneys) is primary heat source via non-shivering thermogenesis.

title: Dehydration — signs of severe
keyPoints: Severe (any 2): lethargy/unconscious, sunken eyes, unable to drink, skin pinch goes back very slowly (>2 s)
Some dehydration (any 2): restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch slow
clinicalContext: 14-mo with diarrhea, lethargic, sunken eyes, unable to drink.
nursingPriority: Severe dehydration — Plan C IV RL 100 mL/kg (30 in 30 min then 70 in 2.5 h), reassess q15-30 min.

title: Hypoxia signs
clinicalContext: Child with SpO2 88%, restless.
nursingPriority: Apply O2 via appropriate device (nasal cannula 1-2 L, mask 5-10 L as needed), reassess SpO2 target >=94%, investigate cause.

title: Cleft lip and palate
keyPoints: Feeding: upright, special bottle (Haberman, Mead Johnson)
Repair: CL at 3 mo (rule of 10s — 10 wk, 10 g Hb, 10 lb wt); CP at 9-18 mo before speech
Post-op: elbow restraints, no pacifier/suction in mouth, logan bow for CL, upright feeds
clinicalContext: Newborn with cleft lip and palate.
nursingPriority: Upright feeding with special bottle, genetic counseling, refer to cleft team, plan surgery per rule of 10s, MDT approach.

title: Hyperthermia — normal room set up
definition: Radiant warmer and neonatal room setup.
clinicalContext: Newborn in radiant warmer with T 37.8.
nursingPriority: Reduce warmer set point, check for overheating, rule out infection (sepsis fever).

title: Meconium aspiration syndrome
definition: Aspiration of meconium-stained liquor causing respiratory distress.
keyPoints: Management: NRP updates: do NOT routinely intubate/suction vigorous meconium-stained babies; intubate only if airway obstruction apparent
Pulmonary hypertension risk; surfactant may help
clinicalContext: Term baby born through thick meconium, not vigorous.
nursingPriority: Resuscitate per NRP: if not breathing/limp, intubate and suction below cords only if airway obstructed; otherwise, standard resuscitation; monitor in NICU.

title: Respiratory distress syndrome
keyPoints: Usually <34 wk; grunting, retractions, tachypnea, nasal flaring
Treatment: antenatal steroids (betamethasone 12 mg IM q24 h x2) if PTL; postnatal: CPAP, surfactant via ETT, avoid oxygen toxicity
clinicalContext: 30-wk preterm with tachypnea and grunting.
nursingPriority: CPAP 5-8 cm, surfactant via INSURE if requirements rising, avoid high FiO2, thermoregulation, IV fluids.

title: Neonatal resuscitation — NRP algorithm
keyPoints: Initial steps <30 s: warm, dry, stimulate, position, clear airway, assess
If HR <100, breathing, crying — assess color, observe
If apnea/gasping or HR <100 — PPV with bag-mask (rate 40-60/min, PIP 20-25 H2O initial)
If HR <60 after 30 s effective PPV — intubate + compressions 3:1 with PPV; 100% O2
clinicalContext: Term baby born apneic, HR 80 at 30 s after initial steps.
nursingPriority: Start PPV at 40-60/min with 21% O2 (term) or 21-30% preterm via bag-mask, reassess in 15 s; escalate if no improvement.

title: Bag-valve-mask ventilation
keyPoints: Size: mask covers mouth + nose, not eyes
C-E grip: thumb + index on mask (C), other 3 fingers on mandible (E)
Rate 40-60/min newborn; volume till chest rises
If not working: MR SOPA — Mask reseal, Reposition airway, Suction, Open mouth, Pressure increase, Airway alternative
clinicalContext: Apneic baby during resuscitation.
nursingPriority: Apply mask with C-E grip, deliver PPV 40-60/min at PIP 20; if chest not rising, run MR SOPA.

title: Moro reflex, creeping, parachute
clinicalContext: 6-mo-old still has strong Moro.
nursingPriority: Persistent primitive reflex — red flag, refer for detailed neurodevelopmental assessment (cerebral palsy risk).

title: Hemorrhagic disease of newborn
definition: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding of newborn.
keyPoints: Late: 2 wk - 6 mo (exclusive BF without vit K, malabsorption)
Prevention: vit K 1 mg IM at birth; low-dose risk late HDN
clinicalContext: Newborn 4 d with umbilical bleeding.
nursingPriority: Suspect classic HDN — vit K 1 mg IM, send PT/INR, fresh frozen plasma if severe bleed, verify vit K was given at birth.

title: Cardio-pulmonary function — good skin colour
keyPoints: Pink skin, warm periphery, capillary refill <2 s
clinicalContext: Child post-sepsis recovery.
nursingPriority: Assess capillary refill, peripheral warmth, pulses, urine output as markers of recovery.

title: Pulse rate of a child (chronologic)
clinicalContext: 3-y-old with HR 180, fever 40.
nursingPriority: Sinus tachycardia in fever; treat fever with paracetamol, hydration, reassess.

title: Cyanotic heart disease — 5 Ts
keyPoints: Newborn cyanosis → prostaglandin E1 to keep ductus patent until surgery
clinicalContext: Newborn with central cyanosis, murmur, no response to O2.
nursingPriority: Suspect cyanotic CHD — start PGE1 infusion 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min, urgent echo, avoid hyperoxia.

title: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)
keyPoints: Machinery murmur, bounding pulses, wide pulse pressure
clinicalContext: Preterm with continuous murmur and bounding pulses.
nursingPriority: Echo to confirm, start ibuprofen closure dose, fluid restriction; if fails, ligation.

title: Cyanosis — central vs peripheral
keyPoints: Peripheral: distal limbs; cold, poor perfusion
Hyperoxia test: central CHD doesn't improve on 100% O2
clinicalContext: Newborn with bluish tongue and lips.
nursingPriority: Central cyanosis — hyperoxia test, echo, rule out cyanotic CHD, start PGE1 if suspected.

title: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF)
keyPoints: Pulmonary stenosis, RVH, VSD, overriding aorta
Tet spells: cyanosis, crying — knee-chest position + O2 + morphine + phenylephrine
clinicalContext: 18-mo with sudden deep cyanosis and crying.
nursingPriority: Tet spell — knee-chest position, 100% O2, morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV, phenylephrine, fluids; plan for early surgical repair.

title: Mitral stenosis
keyPoints: Diastolic rumble, loud S1, opening snap
Left atrial enlargement, AF, systemic embolism
Treatment: balloon valvuloplasty, valve replacement, anticoagulation for AF
clinicalContext: Young female with history of RF, DOE, hemoptysis, AF.
nursingPriority: Mitral stenosis likely; echo, anticoagulate for AF, diuretics for congestion, refer for valvuloplasty.

title: Coarctation of aorta
keyPoints: Upper extremity HTN, lower extremity hypotension
Associations: bicuspid aortic valve, Turner syndrome
Treatment: surgical repair or balloon angioplasty
clinicalContext: Child with HTN in arms, normal BP in legs, rib notching.
nursingPriority: Coarctation — echo, plan surgical or interventional repair, control BP.

title: Site of hematopoiesis (age)
keyPoints: Adult: axial skeleton + proximal long bones
clinicalContext: Adult with marrow reserve query.
nursingPriority: Adult hematopoiesis: vertebrae, sternum, ribs, pelvis, proximal long bones.

title: Hemophilia
keyPoints: Hemarthrosis, deep muscle bleeds, easy bruising
Prolonged aPTT, normal PT, normal platelets, normal BT
Treatment: factor replacement (recombinant), desmopressin for mild A, avoid aspirin/IM injections
clinicalContext: Boy with recurrent knee hemarthrosis.
nursingPriority: Suspect hemophilia — factor VIII/IX assays, avoid IM injections and aspirin, factor replacement, multi-d care, immunize subcutaneously.

title: Leukemia in children
definition: See Medicine-31. Child leukemia typically ALL.
keyPoints: Fatigue, fever, bruising, bone pain, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly
Tumor lysis syndrome risk during induction
Long-term survival ALL ~85% with modern protocols
clinicalContext: Pale irritable 4-y-old with bruises, WBC 100k, blasts 80%.
nursingPriority: Refer pediatric hem-onc, tumor lysis prevention (hydration, allopurinol/rasburicase), infection prophylaxis, central line for induction chemo.

title: Sequestration crisis
definition: Sickle cell — massive splenic pooling of blood — hypovolemic shock.
keyPoints: Children <5 y with sickle cell disease
Treatment: IV fluids, transfusion, splenectomy for recurrent
clinicalContext: Sickle cell 2-y-old with sudden pallor and huge spleen.
nursingPriority: Emergency — IV crystalloid, transfuse packed RBCs, admit to PICU, monitor for splenic recovery; discuss elective splenectomy.

title: Thalassemia major
clinicalContext: Beta thal major child on transfusion.
nursingPriority: Target pre-transfusion Hb 9-10, iron chelation deferasirox, monitor ferritin, HSCT evaluation.

title: Aplastic anemia
keyPoints: Causes: idiopathic (most), drugs (chloramphenicol), radiation, viral (parvo B19, hepatitis)
Treatment: supportive (transfusion, antibiotics), immunosuppression (ATG + cyclosporine), HSCT
clinicalContext: Adolescent with pancytopenia and hypocellular marrow.
nursingPriority: Protective isolation, transfusions as needed, refer for HSCT evaluation, immunosuppressive therapy.

title: Causes of neutropenia
keyPoints: Causes: post-chemo, viral, drugs, cyclic, Kostmann, autoimmune
Febrile neutropenia: blood cultures x2, start broad-spectrum within 1 h (pip-tazo or cefepime)
clinicalContext: Post-chemo patient with ANC 200 and T 38.5.
nursingPriority: Blood cultures from CVC and peripheral, urine, CXR, start IV piperacillin-tazobactam within 1 h, isolate, avoid rectal temp/meds.

title: Meningitis — pediatric
keyPoints: 3 mo-50 y: S pneumoniae, N meningitidis
Empiric <3 mo: ampicillin + cefotaxime; >3 mo: ceftriaxone + vancomycin ± dexamethasone
clinicalContext: 4-y-old with fever, neck stiffness, petechiae.
nursingPriority: Suspect meningococcal — LP urgent, ceftriaxone 80-100 mg/kg/day, droplet isolation, notify, chemoprophylaxis contacts (rifampicin).

title: Spina bifida occulta
definition: Mildest form — vertebral arch defect without herniation.
keyPoints: Usually asymptomatic; tuft of hair, dimple, lipoma over lumbosacral region
clinicalContext: Child with hairy patch on low back.
nursingPriority: Document, refer for spine MRI if any bladder/bowel symptoms, neurosurgical evaluation if tethering.

title: Babinski sign
keyPoints: After 2 y: flexor (downgoing) is normal; extensor = UMN lesion
clinicalContext: 6-mo baby with upgoing Babinski.
nursingPriority: Normal finding; document.

title: Hydrocephalus
definition: CSF accumulation causing ventricular dilation and raised ICP.
keyPoints: Signs infant: bulging fontanel, sunset eyes, increasing head circumference
Cushing triad: HTN + bradycardia + irregular respiration (late)
Treatment: VP shunt, ETV; ensure normal position
clinicalContext: Infant with VP shunt and fever + vomiting.
nursingPriority: Suspect shunt infection/blockage — neurosurgery urgent, CT head, blood/CSF cultures, start empiric antibiotics.

topic: Types of seizures — features and management
title: Types of seizures — features and management
keyPoints: Febrile seizure: 6 mo - 5 y with fever, usually <15 min, generalized; simple vs complex
Avoid sodium valproate in girls of reproductive age
clinicalContext: 18-mo with 3-min generalized seizure during fever.
nursingPriority: Simple febrile seizure — reassure, antipyretic, identify infection source; no need for EEG/neuroimaging; educate parents about recurrence.

title: Post-natal period findings
keyPoints: Vernix caseosa, lanugo, Mongolian spot, milia, erythema toxicum — all normal
clinicalContext: 2-d-old with slate-gray patches on back.
nursingPriority: Mongolian spots — benign, reassure parents, document to avoid later abuse concerns.

title: Neural tube defect — AFP marker
keyPoints: Prevention: folic acid 400 mcg preconception to 12 wk (4 mg if prior NTD)
Covering with sterile saline dressing if open at birth
clinicalContext: Prenatal USG shows myelomeningocele.
nursingPriority: MFM referral, genetic counseling, plan CS, prepare for neurosurgical repair in first 24-48 h of life.

title: Cerebral palsy
definition: Static encephalopathy from perinatal brain insult.
keyPoints: Comorbidities: seizures, intellectual disability, hearing/vision loss, feeding difficulty, contractures
Management: MDT — PT, OT, speech, orthotics, botulinum toxin, baclofen, selective dorsal rhizotomy
clinicalContext: 2-y-old preterm survivor with spastic diplegia.
nursingPriority: MDT referral — PT, OT, speech; orthotics; treat spasticity (oral baclofen/botox); manage comorbidities, caregiver support.

title: Brain tumor in children
definition: Second commonest pediatric cancer after leukemia.
keyPoints: Mostly infratentorial: medulloblastoma, astrocytoma, ependymoma, brainstem glioma
Morning headache with vomiting, ataxia, focal deficits, cranial nerve palsy
clinicalContext: Child with morning vomiting, ataxia, papilledema.
nursingPriority: Urgent MRI — suspect infratentorial tumor; admit, dexamethasone for edema, neurosurgery referral.

title: Craniosynostosis
clinicalContext: Infant with elongated head, palpable ridge.
nursingPriority: Refer for imaging and pediatric neurosurgery; plan cranial remodeling surgery before 1 y.

title: Pyloric stenosis
clinicalContext: Same as surgery entry.
nursingPriority: Correct electrolytes with NS + KCl before surgery; plan pyloromyotomy once corrected.

title: Hirschsprung disease
definition: Congenital absence of ganglion cells in distal bowel.
keyPoints: Failure to pass meconium within 48 h, abdominal distention, bilious vomiting
Rectal biopsy — diagnostic (absence of ganglion cells)
Treatment: definitive pull-through surgery (Duhamel, Soave, Swenson)
Complication: Hirschsprung enterocolitis — fever, distention, explosive stool
clinicalContext: Newborn did not pass meconium in 24 h, distended abdomen.
nursingPriority: Nasogastric decompression, rectal exam reveals explosive decompression (classic), refer pediatric surgery, contrast enema, plan biopsy.

title: Tracheoesophageal fistula
keyPoints: Type C (85%): proximal EA + distal TEF
NG tube coils in upper pouch on X-ray
Copious frothy secretions, coughing-choking with feeds
clinicalContext: Newborn with excessive drooling and coughing on feeding.
nursingPriority: Stop feeds, nasal/oral suction, Replogle tube continuous low-pressure suction of upper pouch, head up 30°, IV fluids, urgent pediatric surgery referral.

title: Normal respiratory rate by age
keyPoints: Newborn 30-60, infant 30-50, toddler 24-40, preschool 22-34, school 18-30, adolescent 12-20
clinicalContext: Newborn RR 50.
nursingPriority: Within normal — document and continue routine care.

title: Primary apnea
definition: Stage of perinatal asphyxia where stimulation restores breathing.
keyPoints: Secondary: PPV needed, no response to stimulation
Clinically indistinguishable at birth; treat all as secondary
clinicalContext: Newborn not breathing after drying and stimulation.
nursingPriority: Assume secondary apnea — start PPV within 60 s of birth, monitor HR, continue algorithm.

title: Croup syndrome
keyPoints: 6 mo - 3 y, barking cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness
Steeple sign on AP neck X-ray
Treatment: humidified O2, dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg single dose, nebulized epinephrine for severe
clinicalContext: 2-y-old with barking cough and stridor at rest.
nursingPriority: Keep calm in parent's lap, humidified O2 if hypoxic, dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM single dose, nebulized epinephrine if severe, observe 4 h after epinephrine.

title: Asthma — pediatric
clinicalContext: 5-y-old with acute wheeze.
nursingPriority: O2 if SpO2 <94%, salbutamol MDI via spacer 2-4 puffs q20 min x3, oral prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg, reassess, admit if incomplete response.

title: Pulmonary atelectasis — lobe involvement
definition: Collapse of lung tissue — decreased gas volume.
keyPoints: Signs: diminished breath sounds, dullness, tracheal shift toward collapse
Treatment: incentive spirometry, chest physiotherapy, bronchoscopy if mucus plug
clinicalContext: Post-op day 2 with dullness right lower zone.
nursingPriority: Incentive spirometry, early ambulation, chest PT, pain control (to aid deep breathing), reassess with CXR.

title: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
definition: Chronic lung disease of preterm (O2 requirement >=28 d at 36 wk PMA).
keyPoints: Prevention: antenatal steroids, gentle ventilation, surfactant, vit A, caffeine
Treatment: diuretics, bronchodilators, steroids (late), O2 at home
clinicalContext: 10-mo ex-28-wk preterm on home O2.
nursingPriority: Continue home O2, monitor growth, RSV prophylaxis palivizumab, feeding support, gradual wean of O2.

title: Juvenile SLE
clinicalContext: Teen girl with malar rash, arthralgia, proteinuria.
nursingPriority: Rheumatology referral, ANA/dsDNA/C3/C4/UA, hydroxychloroquine + prednisolone, sun protection, renal biopsy if nephritis.

title: Skin variations in children
keyPoints: Milia: white pearly papules on nose
clinicalContext: Newborn with erythematous papules 48 h old.
nursingPriority: Erythema toxicum — benign, self-resolves, no treatment.

title: Cradle cap (seborrheic dermatitis)
keyPoints: Treatment: mild shampoo, emollient, gentle brushing, topical antifungal if severe
clinicalContext: 3-mo with thick yellow scales on scalp.
nursingPriority: Reassure; apply baby oil, massage, gentle shampoo; selenium shampoo if persistent.

title: Glomerulonephritis — PSGN
keyPoints: Treatment: supportive — salt + fluid restriction, antihypertensives, penicillin for strep, usually self-limited
clinicalContext: 7-y-old with tea-colored urine, puffy face, HTN 2 wk after throat infection.
nursingPriority: PSGN — salt and fluid restriction, penicillin course to eradicate strep, BP control, monitor for renal failure, usually resolves.

title: Nephrotic syndrome — pediatric
clinicalContext: Same as Medicine-44.
nursingPriority: Prednisolone 60 mg/m2/d, salt restriction, monitor for peritonitis/thrombosis.

title: Ophthalmia neonatorum
keyPoints: Gonococcal day 2-5 (severe, hyperacute, risk of perforation)
clinicalContext: 3-d-old with hyperacute purulent conjunctivitis.
nursingPriority: Suspect gonococcal — ceftriaxone 25-50 mg/kg single IV/IM, saline eye irrigation, isolate; test/treat mother and partner.

title: ADHD
keyPoints: Inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity for >=6 mo in >=2 settings before age 12
Treatment: behavioral therapy, parent training; methylphenidate/atomoxetine
clinicalContext: 7-y-old failing in school, cannot sit still.
nursingPriority: Vanderbilt/Conners assessment, rule out hearing/vision/learning disability, behavioral interventions first-line; stimulants if severe.

title: Kramer rule (neonatal jaundice)
definition: Kramer rule for clinical estimation of neonatal jaundice severity.
keyPoints: Blanch skin over bony prominence with finger pressure
clinicalContext: Day 3 newborn jaundice up to thighs.
nursingPriority: Kramer zone 3 (~12 mg/dL) — plot on Bhutani nomogram for hours of life, consider phototherapy if above threshold, encourage feeding.

title: APGAR scoring
definition: Assessment of newborn at 1 and 5 min.
keyPoints: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration: 0-2 each, total 0-10
Does NOT dictate resuscitation (that is clinical)
Repeat q5 min until >=7 or 20 min
clinicalContext: Newborn with HR 90, weak cry, some flexion, grimace, pink body blue extremities.
nursingPriority: Score A1 P1 G1 A1 R1 = 5 (moderately depressed); continue PPV/suctioning per NRP, reassess q5 min.

title: Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) schedule
definition: Global EPI / India UIP schedule — see chn-1 for details.
keyPoints: 6, 10, 14 wk: OPV, Penta, Rota, fIPV, PCV
clinicalContext: Item on EPI structure.
nursingPriority: Cite India UIP as described, including birth, 6/10/14 wk, 9 mo, and boosters.
